comments.author: indira0003
comments.body:
Did the AI ​​program everything? Or do you need to know how to program for the projects to work? Does the AI ​​make a lot of mistakes? Does it have errors? I've only tried it with Ren'Py, not with Godot.

I don't have high hopes for Godot because I'm just a director giving all the instructions and rules to the AI.

But I'd like to hear about your experience with Godot.  
It really looks incredible.

replies.author: Grobot93
replies.body: AI did all of the coding, I gave all of the instructions and did all of the tuning. I'm not sure if I would say AI really makes any "mistakes." It just does what you tell it to do. If you are not knowledgeable enough or specific enough, it will make assumptions that you may not have intended for it to make. Claude is exceptionally good with GDScript, so as long as you set good foundations, you can build to your heart's content.

comments.author: Luna2442
comments.body: Do you have any advice for your modeling process? I want to generate characters for my game and animate them. Was planning to use meshy but im clueless on how rigging characters for godot works for animations

replies.author: Grobot93
replies.body: I can't really say that my method was particularly good, and especially since the cars don't have any moving parts or really require any animation apart from the front wheels turning, I'm not sure how to offer advice. Claude's models were not particularly great, they just gave me the general shape of the car and they had enough issues that I had to learn how to fix them, and by learning I made some half decent models. Blender YouTube tutorials are great. And Claude can help answer questions on how to accomplish what you want in blender.
